**The Last Letter**

I found the letter in the bottom drawer of my grandfather’s desk, tucked between a yellowed photograph of my mother and a faded newspaper clipping about a storm that had swept through our town years ago. The envelope was brittle, the wax seal cracked, but the paper inside was still crisp—unlike the rest of the house, which smelled of dust and old books.

*Dearest [Name],*

*I write this in the quiet of the night, when the world outside is still and the only sound is the whisper of the wind through the trees. You are far away now, in a place I cannot reach, but I hope this letter finds you when you need it most.*

*I have been thinking about you often lately. About the way you used to laugh at my jokes, even when they were terrible. About the way you would sit with me on the porch, watching the stars, and tell me stories of the universe. You were always so curious, so full of wonder. I wish I could have been more like you—braver, kinder, less afraid of the unknown.*

*But I am not. And that is okay. I have my own battles, my own shadows. The ones you loved were not the ones I was meant to carry. I have spent years trying to be someone I am not, to fit into a life that was never mine. But you, you were always yourself. And that is why I love you. Because you were never afraid to be seen.*

*I do not know what has happened to you. I do not know if you are safe, if you are happy, if you are even alive. But I hope, in some small way, that this letter reaches you. That it reminds you that I was there, that I cared, even when I could not say it aloud.*

*Please, [Name], do not forget me. Do not let the world erase the love we had. It was real. It was beautiful. And it was enough.*

*Forever yours,*
*[His Name]*

I closed the letter, my fingers trembling. The ink was still wet, as if he had written it only moments before. But the paper was old, the words worn. I wondered if he had ever sent it. If he had ever meant to.

Outside, the wind howled, shaking the trees like they were alive. I stood there for a long time, the letter in my hands, the weight of it pressing down on my chest. Then, slowly, I folded it and placed it back in the drawer. Some things were better left unsaid. Some things were better left forgotten.

But I would never forget him. Never forget the love he had given, even in silence.
